$comment: Landing-page demonstration contract. Consumed by src/data/landingDemo.ts and
pinned by backend/tests/testLandingDemoContract.js.
This file is NOT a complete backend AnalysisData payload and must not be typed
as one. It carries exactly two things per scenario:
derivation   - the inputs handed to the real backend guidance contract engine.
presentation - the canonical values the engine derives from those inputs, which
mounted landing components then render verbatim.
The backend test feeds `derivation` to the real buildGuidanceContract and asserts
it produces `presentation.publicLabel`, `presentation.horizonToken` and
`presentation.evidence`. No public verdict wording, horizon vocabulary or risk
threshold is authored here independently of the backend; every canonical value
below is a checked copy of engine output, not a second source of truth.
Purely presentational objects with strict union types (the full Shariah panel and
the thesis-invalidation block) live in landingDemo.ts instead, so TypeScript checks
them against the canonical contract types without a cast. `derivation.shariah`
here is only the two fields the compliance gate reads; a frontend test asserts it
agrees with the rendered panel.
HONEST LIMITATION: `derivation.agreement` is hand-authored. The real agreement
engine derives agreement from nine live indicator services, which a static fixture
cannot run. What is engine-derived is the published verdict - the public label, the
horizon and the evidence presentation - never the starting evidence state. Do not
describe the landing analysis as engine-derived end to end.
There is deliberately no `risk` key anywhere in this file. ComplianceDemo renders
no risk, the real risk engine cannot derive a result from these inputs (no price,
no ATR), and an empty risk object would assert an assessment that was never made.
